name: ESOL
strapline: Your languages are a strength. Make English another tool.
intro: English for Speakers of Other Languages supports learners whose first language is not English. Your existing knowledge and languages matter. Work on a manageable next step in reading, writing, listening or speaking, rather than comparing yourself with someone else. Suggested BGE themes are flexible learning contexts, not a fixed course or a judgement of ability. Your teacher will identify the appropriate qualification level.

bge.title: Finding my way
bge.question: How can I ask for information confidently?
bge.task: Use a fictional school map. Ask how to reach three places and repeat the directions back to check understanding.
bge.extend: Practise “Could you say that more slowly?” and “Do you mean… ?” in a new situation.

bge.title: Learning across subjects
bge.question: How do I explain what I already know?
bge.task: Choose a familiar science or geography idea. Label a diagram, then explain it in four linked sentences. Use your home language to plan if helpful.
bge.extend: Compare a subject word’s everyday meaning and its technical meaning.

bge.title: Everyday choices
bge.question: How do I compare useful information?
bge.task: Compare two fictional travel offers. Identify the destination, time, cost and restrictions, then recommend one for a stated traveller.
bge.extend: Explain a limitation of your recommendation when information is missing.

bge.title: My voice, my story
bge.question: How can I communicate an experience?
bge.task: Write or record a fictional day that went unexpectedly. Include when, where, what changed and how it ended.
bge.extend: Revise one part so a listener can follow the sequence without asking for clarification.

senior.title: ESOL
areas: Work or study contexts as specified
senior.explain: Develop straightforward communication for familiar situations. Placement depends on language learning needs, not age alone.
senior.assessment: Internal unit assessment. Your teacher confirms the correct units and evidence.

senior.title: ESOL
senior.explain: Develop practical language and select information for a purposeful presentation and response to questions. Topic choices are agreed with the assessor.
senior.assessment: Internal units and added value assignment, assessed as pass/fail.

senior.title: ESOL
senior.explain: Understand and use English with increasing independence. Classroom topics support the national language skills; they are not all separate compulsory units.
senior.assessment: Reading, writing and listening question papers and a speaking performance under current guidance.

senior.title: ESOL
areas: Speaking and interaction in everyday, work and study settings
senior.explain: Develop more extended understanding and communication. The department must confirm availability and individual suitability.
senior.assessment: Use the current Higher course and assessment documents on the official ESOL page.

skills.title: Read in stages
skills.explain: Start with the purpose and layout before unknown words.
skills.try: Read a notice for its main message, then locate dates and conditions.
skills.check: Can you explain what action the reader should take?

skills.title: Listen for signposts
skills.explain: Words such as “however” and “finally” show relationships.
skills.try: Listen once for gist, then again for two specific details.
skills.check: Compare your notes with a transcript after your first attempt.

skills.title: Keep a useful vocabulary record
skills.explain: Store a word with its meaning, example and related forms.
skills.check: Can you use the right form in a fresh sentence?

skills.title: Repair communication
skills.explain: Asking for clarification is a skilled response.
skills.try: Practise asking someone to repeat, rephrase or explain a word.
skills.check: Check the meaning back rather than pretending to understand.

practice.question: Read this original notice: “The homework club opens at 3.15 on Tuesdays. Bring your own notes. Places must be booked before noon on Monday.” What must you do before attending?
practice.hint: Find the instruction and its deadline.
practice.answer: Book a place before noon on Monday and bring your notes. The club itself opens on Tuesday at 3.15; do not confuse the booking deadline with the start time.
practice.extend: Write a polite two-sentence booking request using a fictional name.

practice.question: Improve this message: “Need help work. Tomorrow?” Make it clear and polite.
practice.hint: Include who you are asking, what help is needed and a specific request.
practice.answer: For example: “Hello, could you help me understand the graph question? Would it be possible to meet at lunchtime tomorrow?” Clear detail helps the reader respond.
practice.extend: Write a reply explaining that tomorrow is unavailable and offering another time.

practice.question: Read: “Although the bus was late, Hana arrived before the lesson began.” Was Hana late for the lesson? Explain.
practice.hint: “Although” introduces a contrast between the bus and Hana’s arrival.
practice.answer: No. The bus was late, but Hana arrived before the lesson started. The sentence does not tell us exactly how early she arrived.
practice.extend: Rewrite the same meaning using “but”, then explain the punctuation change.

resources.title: British Council LearnEnglish Teens
resources.task: Choose a level-appropriate reading task, attempt the questions and review one error.

resources.title: British Council Video zone
resources.task: Predict the topic, watch once for gist, then use captions or transcript to check three details.

resources.title: British Council general English audio and reading
resources.task: Choose a short audio and note a useful expression you can use tomorrow.

resources.title: Scottish Book Trust learning resources
resources.task: Choose an accessible story resource and retell it with a beginning, change and ending.

resources.title: Qualifications Scotland ESOL
resources.task: Find the correct level with your teacher and use its official learner examples or papers.

ipad.title: A personal language notebook
steps: Choose five words from today’s learning.
Add an English definition, home-language gloss and your own example.
Record pronunciation and revisit the words after a few days.
ipad.evidence: Five words used accurately in a new explanation.

ipad.title: Listen, notice, improve
steps: Record a short explanation of an imagined event.
Listen for one unclear phrase and one missing connection.
Record again and add a transcript.
ipad.evidence: Two versions and a specific note about improvement.

ipad.title: Read a diagram aloud
steps: Label key terms and organise your explanation in numbered steps.
Record while pointing to the relevant parts on screen.
ipad.evidence: A narrated diagram showing subject knowledge and developing English.

careers.title: College and further study
careers.linkToLearning: English supports understanding instructions and sharing subject expertise.
careers.nextStep: Explore college ESOL and vocational pathways with guidance staff.

careers.title: Customer service and hospitality
careers.linkToLearning: Clarifying requests and speaking politely support visitors and colleagues.
careers.nextStep: Compare college hospitality courses and apprenticeships.

careers.title: Health and community roles
careers.linkToLearning: Accurate listening and checking meaning matter in services.
careers.nextStep: Investigate relevant college entry requirements and language support.

careers.title: Your specialist interests
careers.linkToLearning: ESOL can support engineering, creative work, business or university study.
careers.nextStep: Choose an interest and identify the English tasks used in that field.

parentTip: Continue rich conversations and reading in your home language. Ask your young person to explain one new idea in whichever language helps them think, then practise a short English explanation. Progress in English takes time and does not measure intelligence.
